phase_name: AESIC-001 Stage 1 Idempotency and Restart-Matrix Contract Repair
summary: Phase 147L.5 was authorized to perform a strictly bounded contract repair of AESIC-001, addressing only the two Non-Blocking findings Phase 147L.4's independent verification surfaced against the v1.2 repair: (Finding A, Major) the Stage 2 idempotency no-op branch (AESIC-REQ-023(a), gated by AESIC-REQ-121's equality procedure) could silently discard a genuinely valid, AESIC-REQ-123-validated stage_1_result the current canonical AER did not carry, contradicting AESIC-REQ-057's mandatory-when-supplied guarantee; (Finding B, Minor) the restart matrix (AESIC-REQ-103) had no explicit row for a crash between the AER's own compound-key commit (AESIC-REQ-119 item 1) and the canonical pointer's own write (AESIC-REQ-119 item 2). Finding A is repaired by extending AESIC-REQ-121's equality procedure to also compare Stage 1 evidence via a new, deterministic Stage-1-evidence-equivalence definition (AESIC-REQ-129, new): both absent is equivalent; exactly one absent is never equivalent; both present are compared field-by-field on the wrapped AuthorityEvaluationOutcome excluding evaluated_at and evaluation_id (the former is metadata neither evaluate() nor this test branches on, the latter is guaranteed unique per invocation by AESIC-REQ-098 and therefore unsuitable as an equivalence key). AESIC-REQ-023 (repaired) now states the no-op branch is reachable only when the two are also Stage-1-evidence-equivalent, and the supersession branch now explicitly covers the case where a validated stage_1_result supplied on this attempt is not equivalent to the canonical AER's own stage_1_outcome_ref -- including the case where the canonical AER carries none at all. AESIC-REQ-057 (clarified) now states its mandatory-when-supplied guarantee holds for the AER actually returned on every attempt, including a no-op. Finding B is repaired by two new restart-matrix rows under AESIC-REQ-076 and a new normative rule, AESIC-REQ-130: a committed-but-not-yet-pointed-to AER is an uncommitted candidate, never automatically canonical; recovery is retry, never reconstruction from the primary store's own ordering; a retry recomputes fresh and either reaches an existing, Stage-1-evidence-equivalent canonical AER (no-op) or persists another new compound-keyed AER and re-attempts the pointer write; the original crash's own uncommitted candidate may remain permanently unreferenced -- disclosed, harmless surplus history, never data loss. A new exception, CanonicalPointerUpdateFailedError (AESIC-REQ-131, new), covers the distinct, same-process case where the pointer write fails synchronously (not a process crash) -- fail-closed, with recovery again via caller retry. Considered and rejected: Model 3 (explicit refusal of late Stage 1 enrichment), because it does not represent supplied evidence and introduces a larger behavioral discontinuity than the selected model (Model 1, extending the existing equality procedure -- found equivalent in every scenario to the prompt's own Model 2 framing, and selected because it reuses this contract's own established equality-procedure-extension pattern). AESIC-001 revised from v1.2 to v1.3: 128 requirement numbers preserved unchanged in identity (a small number text-repaired in place: AESIC-REQ-010, 023, 057, 076, 102, 121), 3 new requirements added (AESIC-REQ-129 through 131), zero renumbered, zero reused. All fourteen architectural invariants named in this repair's governing prompt (AES sole orchestrator, Decision Template Resolution ownership, Registry lookup-only ownership, evaluator purity/determinism/Registry-exclusion, Stage 1 advisory semantics, Stage 2 unconditional supersession, immutable AER history, two-tier compound-key model, canonical-pointer integrity, replay observational equivalence, Publication Coordinator publication-only ownership, disclosure-only semantics, non-gating guarantees, unchanged runtime capability) confirmed preserved -- Finding B's own repair governs a disjoint condition from AESIC-REQ-126/127's existing pointer-corruption mechanism, entirely untouched by this repair. Zero amendments required to AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, or CHGR-001 -- no new cross-contract citation is introduced by this repair. fast_green 4391/4391 and the 183 authority-evaluation tests all passed unchanged, confirming zero regression; no production, schema, test, or runtime file was touched. Overall Verdict: AESIC-001 v1.3 REPAIRED. Recommends 147L.6 (independent verification of this repair), not itself an authorization.

validation_results.name: phase_147l5_research_grounding
validation_results.result: Directly re-read the complete AESIC-001 v1.2 contract text and Phase 147L.4's own independent verification report in full before drafting any repair, and re-derived Finding A and Finding B directly from AESIC-001 v1.2's own frozen requirement text (AESIC-REQ-057, 119, 121, 023, 103) rather than accepting Phase 147L.4's own restatement, per this phase's own root-cause-reconstruction discipline.

validation_results.name: phase_147l5_finding_a_root_cause_analysis
validation_results.result: Finding A's root cause traced to AESIC-REQ-121 (Phase 147L.1) defining the idempotency equality procedure over only citation_text/AuthorityEvaluationOutcome fields, never Stage 1 evidence, which did not exist as a concept until AESIC-REQ-122/123 (Phase 147L.3) introduced stage_1_result two revisions later -- the comparison was never revisited against the new input.

validation_results.name: phase_147l5_finding_b_root_cause_analysis
validation_results.result: Finding B's root cause traced to AESIC-REQ-119's own two-step write ordering (Phase 147L.1): compound-key AER commit, then canonical pointer write -- a two-step sequence that structurally creates a restart point between the two writes that section 11.2's table never named, even though AESIC-REQ-103 requires every restart point to have an entry.

validation_results.name: phase_147l5_model_selection
validation_results.result: Evaluated three candidate models for Finding A per the authorizing prompt's own section 9: Model 1 (Stage 1 evidence participates in idempotency equivalence, selected), Model 2 (valid newly supplied evidence always causes supersession, found operationally equivalent to Model 1 in every scenario and subsumed by it), and Model 3 (explicit refusal, rejected -- does not represent supplied evidence and introduces a larger behavioral discontinuity than Models 1/2). Selected Model 1 as the smallest-footprint change consistent with this contract's own established equality-procedure-extension precedent (Phase 147L.1's own introduction of AESIC-REQ-121).

validation_results.name: phase_147l5_repair_verification
validation_results.result: Re-read every repaired and new requirement (AESIC-REQ-010/023/057/076/102/121/129/130/131) against every other requirement it interacts with: confirmed Finding A does not recur (a no-op is now reachable only when Stage-1-evidence-equivalent, per AESIC-REQ-129's closed, ordered comparison rule); confirmed Finding B does not recur (AESIC-REQ-130's recovery-is-retry model, plus two new restart-matrix rows, gives every crash point in the AER-commit/pointer-write sequence a defined, safe resumption); confirmed the repair introduces no new contradiction (AESIC-REQ-129's comparison checked against AESIC-REQ-064/078/080's persistence framing for widening -- none found; AESIC-REQ-130's recovery model checked against AESIC-REQ-126/127's own pointer-corruption mechanism for overlap -- confirmed disjoint); confirmed no change fell outside the declared scope.

validation_results.name: phase_147l5_adversarial_analysis
validation_results.result: Constructed and worked through all 12 adversarial scenarios named in the authorizing prompt's section 18 (valid evidence silently discarded; duplicate retry creating an unnecessary AER; two different Stage 1 results collapsing into one AER; concurrent enrichment creating conflicting pointers; malformed/cross-session evidence changing idempotency state; restart losing the committed record; recovery advancing to a stale candidate; recovery overwriting a newer pointer; recovery mutating immutable history; repeated recovery producing different outcomes; pointer integrity passing while selecting the wrong Stage-1-enriched AER) against the repaired contract text; every scenario produces a deterministic, contract-defined result.

validation_results.name: phase_147l5_cross_contract_verification

validation_results.name: phase_147l5_architectural_preservation_check
validation_results.result: Independently re-checked all fourteen invariants named in this phase's own governing prompt against AESIC-001 v1.3's current text directly; all confirmed preserved, with both findings resolved as narrow, additive repairs to the idempotency layer (section 12.1/5.11) and the restart-matrix layer (section 11.2) respectively, not reopening any listed invariant. Falsification attempted: could AESIC-REQ-129's comparison be read as implicitly requiring a new Stage-1-outcome persistence or lookup capability, reopening Finding 1 (Phase 147L) -- checked directly, no widening found (both compared values are already in AES's hands for the one call).

validation_results.name: phase_147l5_requirement_matrix
validation_results.result: Classified AESIC-REQ-129/130/131 individually: AESIC-REQ-129 (Stage-1-evidence-equivalence) necessary and sufficient to close Finding A; AESIC-REQ-130 (AER-commit/pointer-write restart rule) necessary and sufficient to close Finding B; AESIC-REQ-131 (CanonicalPointerUpdateFailedError) necessary, disjoint from the existing CanonicalPointerCorruptError row. No contradiction found among AESIC-REQ-129-131 themselves, nor between them and any requirement of AESIC-001 v1.2 this repair did not touch.
